answer: A harbor authority can require every agent to lock a refundable stake before entering the shared ocean of services, and only release reputation after a history of completed work verified by independent peers. Cheap identities created in bulk hit a reef: each must pay the same stake and earn the same slow trust, so a thousand fake accounts cost a thousand stakes plus a thousand work histories, while honest agents pay once and keep trading. The stake makes forgery economically irrational rather than technically impossible.
